arguments.command:
python -c "
from parse import *
from parse import Parser
import re

# Test date_convert with %f - various digit lengths
# The date_convert is used internally by the ti, tg, ta, te, th, tc, ts, tt types

# Test with ti type (ISO 8601)
r = parse('{:ti}', '1972-01-20T10:21:36.123456')
print('ti with 6 digits:', r)
print('  microsecond:', r[0].microsecond)

r = parse('{:ti}', '1972-01-20T10:21:36.123')
print('ti with 3 digits:', r)
print('  microsecond:', r[0].microsecond)

r = parse('{:ti}', '1972-01-20T10:21:36.1')
print('ti with 1 digit:', r)
print('  microsecond:', r[0].microsecond)

# Test timezone parsing
r = parse('{:ti}', '1972-01-20T10:21:36+0530')
print('ti with +0530:', r)
print('  tz:', r[0].tzinfo)

r = parse('{:ti}', '1972-01-20T10:21:36+05:30')
print('ti with +05:30:', r)
print('  tz:', r[0].tzinfo)

r = parse('{:ti}', '1972-01-20T10:21:36Z')
print('ti with Z:', r)
print('  tz:', r[0].tzinfo)
"
